name: Man or Astro-man?
label: Touch and Go
lede: Auburn students in space jumpsuits swore they were aliens sent to play surf music, then backed it up with tesla coils, six John Peel sessions and a second touring band made of their own clones.

eras.title: Aliens, supposedly, from Auburn
eras.text: Three Auburn University students came up through punk, fell for Dick Dale, The Ventures and the eerie echo of Outer Limits TV, and took stage names and jumpsuits. They never admitted to being human. Inside two years a garage label in Washington State and the BBC were both on board.

years.h: Man or Astro-man? lands in Birmingham, Alabama, for its first show
years.p: Auburn University students Brian Causey (Star Crunch), Brian Teasley (Birdstuff) and Robert Del Bueno (Coco the Electronic Monkey Wizard) play in jumpsuits and keep their real names to themselves.
years.xp:
The name is widely believed to come from the U.S. poster for the 1960 Japanese sci-fi film The Human Vapor, which asked whether its villain was man or astro-man. The band sticks to a story that the members are extraterrestrials, stranded on Earth, who formed a band to research the planet.

Jeff Goodwin joined soon after on second guitar as Dr. Deleto and His Invisible Vapotron.

years.h: The first single, Possession by Remote Control, is an Auburn job
years.p: Homo Habilis Records, a label in the band's home town of Auburn, Alabama, issues the 7" in 1992.

years.h: Is It... Man or Astroman? arrives from a Washington garage label
years.p: Estrus Records of Bellingham puts out the debut LP, and the next two, all stitched together with sound bites from obscure sci-fi films and TV.

years.src: John Peel Wiki · Echoes and Dust
years.h: John Peel gets a postcard from a 19-year-old drummer, then books the band
years.p: Brian Teasley had mailed Peel a card asking him not to play the band. The first session is recorded December 21, 1993 and airs on BBC Radio 1 on January 22, 1994.
years.xp:
Teasley says the card was a hedge against being a one-session wonder: "We didn't want to be a flash in the pan band that did one session and then gets forgotten about forever." It didn't work. By the Peel Wiki's count the band recorded six sessions between 1993 and 2000, and Peel said: "I think I've probably played more records by Man Or Astro-Man? over the last four or five years than anybody else except the Fall."

For one late-1990s session the band swapped Peel's spoken introduction for a robot voice. "We replaced his voice with a robot," Teasley says, using a text-reading program on an Apple Mac. He says Peel kept it on the broadcast.

eras.title: Two more Estrus albums and a lot of road
eras.text: Estrus put out two more records while the band toured nonstop. The UK took to them, and the shows grew into sci-fi stage sets with theremins, oscillators and, eventually, a tesla coil.

years.h: Destroy All Astromen! keeps the formula running
years.p: The second Estrus album mixes early-'60s surf guitar with late-'70s punk and new wave drive, with B-movie dialogue between songs.

years.h: Project Infinity closes the Estrus run
years.p: It's the band's third and last Estrus album of the first run. The same year Live Transmissions from Uranus comes out on One Louder and Homo Habilis.

years.src: John Peel Wiki · Echoes and Dust
years.h: John Peel spends the Phoenix Festival hanging out with the band
years.p: Brian Teasley says Peel found them funny. The band's second Peel session, recorded March 19, had aired that April.
years.xp: At England's Phoenix Festival in 1995, Teasley says, Peel spent time with the band. The second session included a track titled "Inside the Head of Mr John Peel". By the Peel Wiki's list, the band named tracks after him in three different sessions.

years.cap: Coco and Star Crunch on stage at the Met Cafe, Providence, September 1996
years.h: A Welsh band stops a Newport show to rescue the merch money
years.p: At TJ's in Newport, the pouch of money slid off Brian Teasley's bass drum into the crowd. The Cowboy Killers stopped everything to help get it back.

eras.title: Touch and Go takes them in, and the band copies itself
eras.text: Touch and Go signed the band in 1996 and the records got stranger and more electronic. Cartoon Network hired them, Star Crunch walked out, and the others answered by training two extra touring versions of themselves.

yt: Live at Lee's Palace, Toronto, December 8, 1996
years.h: Experiment Zero brings the band to Touch and Go
years.p: The Chicago label becomes Man or Astro-man?'s home. Two more 1996 albums follow elsewhere: What Remains Inside a Black Hole (Au Go Go) and Intravenous Television Continuum (One Louder).

years.h: Peel session number three ends up in his own best-of
years.p: Recorded June 11, 1996 and broadcast July 13, it is later picked for Peel Sessions: The Best 125.
years.xp: The session opened with a track named for the host, "Welcome to the Wicky Wacky World of John Peel", and ran through "The Man Made of CO2", "9 Volt" and "Television Fission".

years.h: Made from Technetium leans further into synths
years.p: The band's second Touch and Go album is co-released with One Louder and Au Go Go.

years.h: The band writes the closing theme for Space Ghost Coast to Coast
years.p: For the 1997 season of Cartoon Network's show it also records the interstitial music. The main theme isn't theirs: it's credited to [[Sonny Sharrock|ebd39596-e2bb-4b3c-a661-412a4198a083]].

years.cap: Star Crunch on guitar at the Met Cafe, Providence, September 1996
years.h: Star Crunch quits to run a record label
years.p: Brian Causey goes on to write and perform the theme for Nickelodeon's The Adventures of Jimmy Neutron and to run Warm Electronic Recordings in Athens, Georgia.
years.xp: The others carried on with musicians from the clone projects. According to Rock and Roll Globe, the line-up that made A Spectrum of Infinite Scale came straight out of them.

years.big: We did it because we were fucking crazy
years.src: Wikipedia · Encyclopedia of Alabama · Echoes and Dust
years.h: A second Man or Astro-man? goes on the road as Clone Project Alpha
years.p: The band trains a whole second band as renamed doubles of each member (Dorkstuff, Cocoid, Chromo Crunch and Dexter Y). Brian Teasley on why, in 2025:
years.xp:
A second clone band, Clone Project Gamma, followed with an all-female line-up: Coco Active (Shonali Bhowmik), Chromia Staria (Deb Davis), Tweety-Tone (Ani Cordero) and Carol ([[Shannon Wright|d5fd4600-318d-457b-9cbb-b74633c51ed5]]). Teasley calls the whole thing the Astro-man Genome Project.

He admits fans first called it a cash grab. Now, he says, people claim to have been at shows they probably missed.

eras.title: Two clones join, then the power goes off
eras.text: Blazar the Probe Handler and Trace Reading, both recruited from the clone projects, joined the real band. They made a record with Steve Albini, toured it, and then switched the whole thing off.

yt: The Beat Room, G7 Glasgow, BBC Choice Scotland, 1999
years.h: EEVIAC Operational Index and Reference Guide invents a computer
years.p: The concept album about an imaginary machine comes out on Touch and Go and Epitaph Europe, made by the post-Star Crunch line-up. The band's fifth Peel session airs in July.

q: We weren't afraid to be thought of as good musicians
years.h: Steve Albini records A Spectrum of Infinite Scale at Zero Return
years.p: Birdstuff, Coco, Blazar the Probe Handler (Richie Edelson) and Trace Reading (Erich Hubner) cut it in Atlanta. The last two came over from the clone projects.
years.xp:
Rock and Roll Globe says the studio was brand new and that the band's own account of the control room is two shipping containers welded together and hauled onto concrete pillars by forklift. Of Albini, Teasley says: "He was always like the older kid to us."

Looking back on the record, Teasley said the band had stopped hiding behind the kitsch and let the playing show.

years.h: The sixth Peel session goes out live from Maida Vale
years.p: The BBC broadcasts the band's last session for John Peel from its Maida Vale studios on November 1, 2000, with "Theme from Eeviac" and "Television Fission" in the set.

years.cap: The tesla coil at a club show, around 2002
years.src: Encyclopedia of Alabama · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Man or Astro-man? stops touring after roughly 1,500 shows
years.p: The Spectrum tour, sold with the tour-only A Spectrum of Finite Scale, is the last for a long while. The Encyclopedia of Alabama counts over 1,500 shows in 31 countries since 1993.
years.xp:
The biggest crowd, the Encyclopedia of Alabama says, was 40,000 people at the Lowlands festival in the Netherlands. The smallest was two people, at an in-store in southern Australia. Teasley's own count in 2025 is bigger: "two thousand shows in forty plus countries," with more than two years of his life spent in the UK.

Estrus put out Beyond the Black Hole the same year.

eras.title: The astromen touch down again
eras.text: The original trio came back for a hometown show and Touch and Go's 25th birthday, then kept returning. Teasley spent the break drumming for St. Vincent and The Polyphonic Spree and running a Birmingham club.

years.cap: Keytar and a red jumpsuit at the 2006 reunion shows
years.h: The original lineup reunites at Birmingham's Bottletree Café
years.p: Star Crunch, Birdstuff and Coco, plus Jeff Goodwin as Dr. Deleto, play the club Brian Teasley ran until it closed in 2015.

years.cap: The tesla coil at the 2006 reunion shows
years.h: Touch and Go turns 25 and Birdstuff gives his drums to the crowd
years.p: The anniversary weekend in Chicago gets 45 minutes with a tesla coil, after which Brian Teasley hands most of his kit to stunned fans.

years.cap: Man or Astro-man? at Cat's Cradle, Carrboro, North Carolina, November 2010
years.h: The trio books Whirly Ball, the Bottletree and South by Southwest
years.p: The 2010 dates cover Atlanta, Birmingham and Austin, then Toronto's NXNE festival in June.

years.cap: The tesla coil at Cat's Cradle, Carrboro, North Carolina, November 2010
years.h: Samantha Paulsen becomes the first woman in Man or Astro-man?
years.p: As Avona Nova she joins on guitar, replacing Victor Vector (Jonny Browning, 2010-11).

years.h: First new music in 12 years: Defcon 5...4...3...2...1
years.p: The comeback record comes out on Causey's Warm Electronic Recordings and on Chunklet Industries.

eras.title: On its own clock
eras.text: Man or Astro-man? now plays when it likes. Jack White's Nashville label put out the live record, the Peel sessions came back on vinyl, and the drummer owns a club.

years.cap: The four members in an Astro Industries quarantine booth, promo shot, 2018
years.h: Live at Third Man Records is cut for Jack White's label
years.p: Chunklet Industries later reissues the band's BBC sessions, including ROYGBIV (Recordings from the BBC).

yt: Alabama Public Television feature on Brian Teasley
years.h: Teasley says about 70 songs sit unfinished
years.p: He owns the Saturn club in Birmingham, Alabama, and tells Echoes and Dust the band plays when it feels like it.
years.xp: "We probably got seventy songs that aren't finished there," Teasley says, blaming "the greater world at large." Besides Saturn, he is helping with an amphitheater in Huntsville, where NASA is based.
